subject: Computer Networking
title: HTTP — The Web's Protocol
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on HTTP — The Web's Protocol.

hook.text: When you click a link, your browser sends an HTTP request. The server sends back an HTTP response. That's the web.

buildup.text: HTTP methods define actions: GET fetches data, POST submits data, PUT updates, DELETE removes.

discovery.text: Status codes tell the outcome: 200 OK, 301 Moved, 404 Not Found, 500 Server Error.

twist.text: HTTP is stateless. The server forgets you after each request. Cookies are the workaround for sessions.

climax.text: Headers carry metadata: content type, caching rules, auth tokens. They're invisible but control everything.

punchline.text: HTTP is request and response. The simplest protocol that runs the web.

quiz.question: Why is HTTP called stateless?
options: The server does not remember previous requests
It cannot transfer files larger than 1 MB
It only works over wireless connections

details.summary: HTTP defines how web browsers request resources from servers and how servers respond. It uses a simple request-response model with methods, headers, status codes, and body content. HTTP is stateless — each request is independent, with cookies and tokens adding statefulness when needed.
details.whyItMatters: HTTP is the protocol underlying all web communication. Understanding its request-response model, methods, and status codes is essential for web development and API design.
takeaways: HTTP uses a request-response model with methods and status codes
Headers carry metadata like content type and authentication tokens
Stateless design enables simple scaling across many servers

faq.question: What do HTTP status codes mean?
faq.answer: 200 series indicates success. 301 and 302 are redirects. 400 means bad request, 401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden, 404 not found. 500 series indicates server errors. Status codes tell the client whether the request succeeded and what to do next if it did not.

faq.question: What are HTTP headers used for?
faq.answer: Headers carry metadata about the request or response. Content-Type specifies the data format. Authorization carries authentication credentials. Cache-Control directs caching behavior. Custom headers exchange application-specific information. Headers are key-value pairs sent before the body.
